_comment: Canonical PromQL for AG-Sept PR2. This file is the single source: the Grafana dashboard
and the snapshot exporter are both generated from it, so the panel an operator watched and
the CSV the report quotes cannot drift apart. TestDashboardMatchesCanonicalPanels enforces
that. Change an expression here, not in the dashboard JSON.
RANGE TOKEN. Range selectors are written as $RANGE rather than as Grafana's
$__rate_interval, because that macro is a Grafana construct the Prometheus HTTP API cannot
parse — an exporter would have to rewrite the expression, and a rewritten expression is no
longer the same query source. $RANGE is repository-owned and each consumer substitutes it:
Grafana   -> $__rate_interval   (adaptive; Grafana knows the panel's resolution)
exporter  -> a literal window, recorded per cell alongside the CSV
The exporter records the value it used because a rate over 5s and a rate over 60s are
different measurements, and a CSV that does not say which is not reproducible.
Scope is measurement-contract §6's required indicators and nothing else.

panels.title: Successful mutation goodput
panels._note: Mutations only, never list_slots (observability §3.1), and replay=false only: a replay returns a recorded outcome without performing a mutation (measurement-contract §4.2), so counting it would overstate useful work and count one booking twice. Same definition as Summary.Goodput and as the FreshAdmittedFor count reconciliation compares against persisted rows.

panels.title: Replayed mutations
panels._note: The population goodput excludes, shown rather than dropped. A replay is a correctness claim in its own right (INV-5); the `replay` workload is what verifies it.

panels.title: Request latency p50
panels._note: Required by measurement-contract §6, and it is an SLO gate (measurement-contract §7: p50 <= 50ms). SLO-safe capacity is the highest goodput satisfying *all* latency gates, so a panel set without p50 cannot evaluate one of the three.

panels.title: Outcomes
panels._note: Business refusals are a valid domain answer and are reported separately here, never folded into a failure rate (measurement-contract §3).

panels.title: DB pool connections held
panels._note: The pool's actual population, which is NOT its maximum. Reading a fall in `pool_in_use` against `pool_max` as connections being withheld requires this series to say the connections existed: max is a ceiling. AG-Sept PR4a §3.13.1 is the worked example.

panels.title: DB pool connections idle
panels._note: Idle sitting at zero with in-use at the ceiling is a saturated pool. Idle staying high while acquire cost rises is not pool exhaustion, and points at the acquire path instead.

panels.title: DB pool acquire duration
panels._note: Seconds of *total Acquire() duration* accumulated per second — NOT queueing time, despite the metric's name. pgxpool times the whole call, including constructing a new connection, so this rises when acquiring is slow for any reason. It does not license 'the pool is the frontier' on its own; read it with pool_empty_acquire_wait and pool_new_conns, and use pool_acquire_mean for per-acquire cost.

panels.title: DB pool empty-acquire time
panels._note: Time on acquires that found no idle connection. NOT pure contention: puddle accumulates both waiting for a connection to be released AND constructing a new one here, and construction time is included in full. Separate them with pool_new_conns — rising together implicates construction/churn; empty-wait rising while new-conns stays flat means acquires waited on existing connections. pool_acquire_wait rising while this stays flat puts the delay elsewhere in the immediate acquire path.

panels.title: DB pool mean acquire duration
panels._note: Per-acquire cost, rate(duration)/rate(count). The aggregate rate confounds cost with acquire volume: a cell doing half the work at twice the cost can show an unchanged total. §3.13.1's 16x rise is this series, not the aggregate.

panels.title: DB pool connections established
panels._note: Connection constructions started per second. Construction calls pgx.ConnectConfig, so this is real establishment against PostgreSQL — network, TLS and authentication. It is the series that separates the two things pool_empty_acquire_wait conflates, and the reason 'the symptom is in the acquire path' does not exclude PostgreSQL: construction is where PostgreSQL enters that path.

panels.title: Process CPU
panels._note: JOB-SCOPED, and every panel below it for the same reason. process_* and go_* are exported by *every* Prometheus-instrumented Go process — node_exporter and Prometheus itself included — so an unscoped selector means "the service" only while exactly one job is scraped. Adding the host job would otherwise fold three processes into a panel titled for one, and nothing would report it: the CSV still exports, still carries rows, and still passes the populated-series gate.

panels.title: GC pause quantile
panels._note: The Go collector exports this as a summary, so the series carries its own quantile label rather than needing histogram_quantile.

_export_range_note: The window the exporter substitutes for $RANGE unless a cell overrides it. Must be at least 4x prometheus.yml's scrape_interval (1s) for rate() to have enough points to be stable; 15s gives 15, which smooths a sweep cell without hiding the knee a frontier is read from.
